$comment: Single source of truth for what this companion release is qualified against. Read by the DSH adapter, the runtime staging script, the coupling gate, and the compatibility probes. Changing a pinned value requires re-running the per-platform qualification lanes.

readinessAdapter.$comment: Parses the official stdout ready line 'dsh web: <url>'. Captured from the tested release; see packages/dsh-adapter/src/readiness.ts.

profile.name: desktop
profile.$supersededScopesNote: Package scopes this distribution published under before. A profile left by one of those releases still names its bundle layers and still has its packages installed, so neither the layer list nor node_modules can tell the difference from a layer the user added. Listing the scopes is the only auditable way to say "this was us"; provisioning drops layers in these scopes and reinstalls the current ones.

acceptanceRule: A target is accepted only after its workflow, security, compatibility, performance, native-operation, and process-quiescence lanes pass on a real host of that platform. Cross-build, emulation, and Wine results are never acceptance.

packageManager.name: pnpm
packageManager.reason: The official dsh plugin command forwards to pnpm on PATH. A packaged application launched from the desktop has a minimal PATH, so the package manager ships with the stage.

minimalIdentity.note: Derived at runtime via agentPresets.mount + tools.schemas(agent) + systemPrompt.assemble({scope:agent}). This record is an observation bound to the exact DSH version, never a source of truth: a mismatch means re-derive and re-qualify, not edit this file.
